teaching_point: Ulcerated BCC on the nose. A non-healing, picked, slowly enlarging facial ulcer in an older adult is BCC until proven otherwise.
dermnet_caption: Basal cell carcinoma affecting the nose
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Basal cell carcinoma affecting the nose (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/basal-cell-carcinoma-affecting-the-nose-images

teaching_point: Typical ulcerated nodular BCC: pearly rolled edge, broken telangiectasia, central ulcer/crust ('rodent ulcer'). These are NG12 1.7.5 features (non-urgent referral).
dermnet_caption: A typical ulcerated nodular basal cell carcinoma - note the pearly appearence and broken telangiectatic vessels
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A typical ulcerated nodular basal cell carcinoma - note the pearly appearence and broken telangiectatic vessels (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Nodular BCC on the forehead: raised pearly edge with telangiectasia over it.
dermnet_caption: A nodular basal cell carcinoma on the forehead - note the raised pearly edge, telangiectasia, and central depression
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A nodular basal cell carcinoma on the forehead - note the raised pearly edge, telangiectasia, and central depression (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Advanced, neglected BCC around the eye. Periocular or large lesions are where NG12 1.7.6 allows a suspected cancer pathway referral because delay matters. This is relevant to care-home residents who cannot self-report.
dermnet_caption: An advanced and neglected basal cell carcinoma on the eyelid
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — An advanced and neglected basal cell carcinoma on the eyelid (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Pigmented nodular BCC in skin of colour. BCC is often pigmented in darker skin types and can be mistaken for melanoma or SK.
dermnet_caption: A nodular pigmented basal cell carcinoma in a Māori patient
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A nodular pigmented basal cell carcinoma in a Māori patient (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Superficial BCC: slowly spreading, well-marginated pink scaly plaque with a thread-like edge, usually on the trunk. Specialist options include imiquimod, 5-FU, PDT, curettage or cryotherapy.
dermnet_caption: A slowly-spreading pink and well-marginated superficial basal cell carcinoma
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A slowly-spreading pink and well-marginated superficial basal cell carcinoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Morphoeic (infiltrative) BCC: scar-like, waxy, ill-defined with branched telangiectasia. This is high-risk in BAD 2021, and Mohs surgery is often considered.
dermnet_caption: A morphoeic basal cell carcinoma on the lip - note the branched telangiectasia within the scar-like lesion
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A morphoeic basal cell carcinoma on the lip - note the branched telangiectasia within the scar-like lesion (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Pigmented BCC on the nose. If you cannot confidently exclude melanoma, refer using the melanoma criteria (weighted 7-point checklist).
dermnet_caption: A pigmented basal cell carcinoma on the nose
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A pigmented basal cell carcinoma on the nose (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: sharply focused, broken arborising (tree-like) telangiectasia with central white structureless areas. This is the key BCC vessel pattern.
dermnet_caption: Dermoscopy shows the broken arborising telangiectasia and central featureless sclerosis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy shows the broken arborising telangiectasia and central featureless sclerosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of pigmented BCC: blue-grey ovoid nests and globules.
dermnet_caption: Blue-grey ovoid nests in pigmented basal cell carcinoma dermoscopy
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Blue-grey ovoid nests in pigmented basal cell carcinoma dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/basal-cell-carcinoma-dermoscopy

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of pigmented BCC: spoke-wheel and leaf-like structures.
dermnet_caption: Spoke wheels in pigmented basal cell carcinoma dermoscopy
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Spoke wheels in pigmented basal cell carcinoma dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/basal-cell-carcinoma-dermoscopy

teaching_point: Histology of nodular BCC: nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction clefts.
dermnet_caption: A nodular basal cell carcinoma - the peripheral palisading of the basaloid cells can be appreciated
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A nodular basal cell carcinoma - the peripheral palisading of the basaloid cells can be appreciated (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/basal-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Trigeminal trophic syndrome: crescent-shaped ulcer and tissue loss of the nasal ala from repeated picking of numb skin (after stroke or trigeminal injury).
dermnet_caption: Loss of the ala nasi from picking in trigeminal trophic syndrome
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Loss of the ala nasi from picking in trigeminal trophic syndrome (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trigeminal-trophic-syndrome

teaching_point: Excoriation of the ala in trigeminal trophic syndrome. Clues are a history of stroke or trigeminal procedure, numbness or paraesthesia, and self-manipulation.
dermnet_caption: Excoriation of the ala nasi in trigeminal trophic syndrome
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Excoriation of the ala nasi in trigeminal trophic syndrome (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trigeminal-trophic-syndrome

teaching_point: Gorlin (basal cell naevus) syndrome: multiple BCCs and surgical scars from an early age (PTCH1, hedgehog pathway). Avoid radiotherapy; genetics referral; family screening.
dermnet_caption: Multiple BCCs and scars
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Multiple BCCs and scars (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/basal-cell-naevus-syndrome

teaching_point: Palmar pits in Gorlin syndrome. Other clues are jaw (odontogenic) keratocysts, bifid ribs, calcified falx and macrocephaly.
dermnet_caption: Palmar pits
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Palmar pits (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/basal-cell-naevus-syndrome

teaching_point: Ulcerated, firm lower-lip lesion in a smoker = SCC. Induration is the first sign of malignancy. The lip is a high-risk site, so make a suspected cancer pathway referral (NG12 1.7.4).
dermnet_caption: An ulcerated and firm lesion on the lip - the patient was a smoker and the lesion was a squamous cell carcinoma
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — An ulcerated and firm lesion on the lip - the patient was a smoker and the lesion was a squamous cell carcinoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-squamous-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Bleeding ulcerated poorly differentiated SCC on the ear: high-risk site and histology (BAD 2020).
dermnet_caption: A bleeding and ulcerated poorly-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma on the ear
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A bleeding and ulcerated poorly-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma on the ear (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-squamous-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Ulcerated ear SCC with an enlarged pre-auricular lymph node. Always examine the regional nodes; a palpable node means urgent referral (possible nodal metastasis).
dermnet_caption: An ulcerated squamous cell carcinoma on the ear; there is enlargement of the pre-auricular lymph node due to spread of the tumour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — An ulcerated squamous cell carcinoma on the ear; there is enlargement of the pre-auricular lymph node due to spread of the tumour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-squamous-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Cutaneous horn: a keratin projection that can sit on a wart, AK, SCC or KA. The base must be examined histologically, so never just clip it off.
dermnet_caption: Cutaneous horn
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous horn (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-squamous-cell-carcinoma

teaching_point: SCC arising in a long-standing leg ulcer (Marjolin ulcer). Exuberant granulation, a rolled edge or a non-healing area in a chronic wound needs biopsy.
dermnet_caption: A squamous cell carcinoma has arisen within a longstanding venous ulcer
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A squamous cell carcinoma has arisen within a longstanding venous ulcer (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/cutaneous-squamous-cell-carcinoma-images

teaching_point: Carcinoma cuniculatum: the plantar form of verrucous carcinoma, a slow, warty, locally destructive well-differentiated SCC. A 'plantar wart' that is enlarging or destructive in an adult needs referral.
dermnet_caption: Carcinoma cuniculatum
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Carcinoma cuniculatum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-squamous-cell-carcinoma

teaching_point: Actinic cheilitis: dry, scaly, blurred vermilion border of the lower lip (AK of the lip). Lip SCC usually arises here. Refer if it is persistent, thickened, ulcerated or tender.
dermnet_caption: Actinic cheilitis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Actinic cheilitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/actinic-cheilitis

teaching_point: Bowen's disease (SCC in situ) on a finger: a persistent, well-demarcated, scaly red plaque. Lesions on digits, nail or genitals go to a specialist; it is often treated with 5-FU, cryotherapy, PDT or excision.
dermnet_caption: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Squamous cell carcinoma in situ (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/intraepidermal-squamous-cell-carcinoma

teaching_point: Patches and plaques of mycosis fungoides on the trunk. A fixed, 'eczema-like' rash in sun-protected sites that fails steroids for months needs biopsy.
dermnet_caption: Patches and plaques of mycosis fungoides
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Patches and plaques of mycosis fungoides (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mycosis-fungoides

teaching_point: Plaque-stage MF: variable-sized, sharply defined red-brown plaques. Often several biopsies off treatment are needed (ISCL criteria).
dermnet_caption: Plaque stage mycosis fungoides
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Plaque stage mycosis fungoides (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mycosis-fungoides

teaching_point: Tumour-stage CTCL: an ulcerated nodule arising in long-standing MF (stage IIB). Needs urgent specialist (CTCL MDT) care.
dermnet_caption: Tumour stage of CTCL
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Tumour stage of CTCL (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-t-cell-lymphoma

teaching_point: Sézary syndrome: erythroderma with circulating malignant T cells (lymphadenopathy, palmoplantar keratoderma, severe itch). Erythroderma means same-day or urgent specialist assessment.
dermnet_caption: Sézary syndrome
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Sézary syndrome (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-t-cell-lymphoma

teaching_point: MF histology: atypical lymphocytes in the epidermis (epidermotropism) forming Pautrier microabscesses.
dermnet_caption: Mycosis fungoides, histology
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mycosis fungoides, histology (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mycosis-fungoides
